verdict.rationale: Sentry's API docs refer to organizations having a 'region-specific domain', which implies multi-region hosting. Sentry also officially documents a self-hosted deployment that runs entirely on your own server, so you control where data lives; a community user confirms running it in production. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of choosing a SaaS data-storage region (e.g. US vs EU) at signup or per org, named data-residency guarantees, and documentation of migrating between regions.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: Using your organization's region-specific domain will generally result in lower latency for most API calls.
How you can run all of Sentry on your own server, without paying anything.
They have run self-hosted Sentry at work for a couple of years and it has worked fantastically; once running it is rock-solid.
